analysis.summary: Kubernetes v1.37.0 是一个包含重要API变更、性能改进和关键Bug修复的版本，重点关注存储（SELinuxMount GA）、调度API升级和稳定性提升，但包含多个需要立即关注的破坏性变更。
key_changes: SELinuxMount 功能门升级至 GA 并默认启用，可能破坏启用 SELinux 集群中的现有工作负载 - [PR #139956](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139956) - **影响：** 启用 SELinux 的集群中，现有 Pod 可能因卷标签不匹配而无法启动，需在升级前评估和修复。
scheduling.k8s.io API 组从 v1alpha2 升级到 v1alpha3，并完全移除 v1alpha2 - [PR #138572](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138572) - **影响：** 所有 v1alpha2 对象必须在升级前从 API Server 中删除，否则升级将失败。
修复 kubelet 配置 eventRecordQPS 设置为 0 时仍有限制的问题 - [PR #117119](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117119) - **影响：** 之前设置为 0 表示“无限制”，但实际限制为 5 QPS，修复后行为符合预期。
StatefulSet 新增 Recreate 更新策略 - [PR #137187](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137187) - **影响：** 为有状态应用提供了类似 Deployment 的重建更新方式，增强了更新灵活性。
引入声明式的 EvictionRequest API 用于 Pod 优雅驱逐 - [PR #137050](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137050) - **影响：** 提供了更可控的 Pod 驱逐机制，可用于构建自定义的节点排空和工作负载管理工具。
important_bugfixes: 修复 StatefulSet 使用 OnDelete 策略时 CurrentRevision 不更新的问题 - [PR #136833](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136833) - **影响：** 修复了长期存在的 Bug，确保状态准确反映当前版本，影响所有使用 OnDelete 策略的 StatefulSet。
修复 CronJob 控制器在获取现有 Job 时使用空命名空间的问题 - [PR #136920](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136920) - **影响：** 修复了 CronJob 控制器无法正确采用现有 Job 的问题，可能导致 Job 重复创建或状态不一致。
修复节点关机管理器中导致线程耗尽的 dbus 连接泄漏 - [PR #137141](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137141) - **影响：** 防止因连接泄漏导致 kubelet 线程耗尽并崩溃，提升节点稳定性。
修复 kubectl drain --disable-eviction --dry-run=server 命令无限挂起的问题 - [PR #137543](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137543) - **影响：** 修复了 drain 命令在特定参数组合下的阻塞问题，影响运维操作。
修复 Binding API 不验证节点名称导致 Pod 卡在删除状态的问题 - [PR #136776](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136776) - **影响：** 防止绑定到无效节点名的 Pod 因终结器而无法删除，需手动介入清理。
修复 ImageVolume 验证允许空引用导致运行时失败的问题 - [PR #135989](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135989) - **影响：** API 验证通过但 Pod 创建失败，修复后提前在 API 层拒绝无效配置。
security_issues: 未在此版本发布说明中识别到公开的 CVE 或高危安全问题。但条件授权机制的引入（Conditional Authz）可能影响现有的授权策略评估逻辑，建议审查 - [PR #137513](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137513) - **风险级别：** 低
performance_improvements: kube-proxy 在 nftables 模式下默认启用 netlink 支持以提升性能 - [PR #137536](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137536) - **提升：** 通过直接使用 netlink 列出规则，避免执行和解析 `nft` 命令行二进制文件，提升规则处理性能。
引入 EtcdRangeStream Beta 功能门，优化 watch 缓存初始化 - [PR #136915](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136915) - **提升：** 通过单次流式 RPC 而非分页请求初始化 watch 缓存，显著减少大型集群的 API Server 启动时间。
优化 GangScheduling 插件的事件处理，减少不必要的队列提示函数执行 - [PR #135905](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135905) - **提升：** 减少调度器在 Pod 添加事件时的无效处理开销，提升调度性能。

多项指标从 Alpha 升级到 Beta，提供更强的稳定性保证 - [PR #136189](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136189), [PR #137072](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137072), [PR #136894](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136894) - **提升：** 为存储操作、ServiceAccount Token 和工具类指标提供稳定的监控数据源。
breaking_changes: scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2 API 版本被移除 - [PR #138572](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138572) - **影响：** 升级前必须使用 kubectl 或 API 删除所有 v1alpha2 对象（如 Workload, PodGroup），否则 kube-apiserver 将无法启动。
SELinuxMount 功能门默认启用且无法禁用 - [PR #139956](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139956) - **影响：** 在启用 SELinux 的集群中，任何依赖旧卷挂载行为的 Pod 可能无法启动。必须按照官方博客指南预先识别和修复问题工作负载。
client-go 中广泛移除 context.TODO()，引入新的上下文感知 API - [PR #129125](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129125) - **影响：** 直接使用 client-go 底层接口的应用程序可能需要更新代码以传递上下文，否则可能遇到编译错误或警告。
移除未使用的 PodStatusResult 类型 - [PR #136271](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136271) - **影响：** 任何直接导入此内部类型的代码将无法编译，但该类型从未在公共 API 中使用，影响范围有限。
废弃并锁定 DeclarativeValidationTakeover 功能门 - [PR #139212](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139212) - **影响：** 该功能门被锁定为默认值，显式启用或禁用它将不再生效，需移除相关配置。
recommendations: **升级前必须操作：** 1) 如果集群启用 SELinux，务必阅读官方博客并运行检测工具，修复或豁免受影响的工作负载。2) 清理所有 scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2 资源对象。
**测试建议：** 在非生产环境充分测试，重点验证：1) 所有 StatefulSet（特别是使用 OnDelete 策略的）的状态更新。2) CronJob 的 Job 创建和管理。3) 使用自定义调度器或 Binding API 的流程。
**客户端更新：** 检查并更新所有使用 client-go 库的应用程序、控制器或工具，确保它们能适配新的上下文感知 API。
**监控与观察：** 升级后，密切关注 kubelet 事件速率限制、kube-proxy 在 nftables 模式下的性能，以及 API Server 的 watch 缓存初始化时间。
**配置清理：** 从 kubeadm 配置、kubelet 配置文件和功能门列表中移除已锁定或删除的配置项，如 DeclarativeValidationTakeover 和 AnyVolumeDataSource。
**长期规划：** 注意 kubectl run --filename/-f 标志已被废弃，未来版本将移除，应迁移到 kubectl create -f 或 kubectl apply -f。
analysis.risk_assessment: **整体风险评估：中等偏高**。此版本包含两个高影响的破坏性变更（SELinuxMount GA 和 v1alpha2 API 移除），处理不当可直接导致集群升级失败或工作负载中断。然而，它也修复了多个影响稳定性的关键 Bug（如 StatefulSet 状态、CronJob 控制器、kubelet 连接泄漏）。建议的升级时机是在充分测试后，选择维护窗口进行。需要特别关注的方面包括：SELinux 环境兼容性、遗留的 v1alpha2 对象清理、client-go 依赖项的兼容性，以及所有有状态工作负载（StatefulSet、CronJob）升级后的行为验证。

139837.title: Dump full config on kubelet startup instead of command line arguments
139837.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

/sig node

Dump the full effective KubeletConfiguration at startup. Printing the raw command-line flags (cliflag.PrintFlags, below) is misleading: flags that mirror KubeletConfiguration fields are parsed before --config / --config-dir are merged and flag precedence is re-enforced, so they can show stale values that do not match what the kubelet actually runs with. The effective configuration logged here reflects all overrides (defaults, the --config file, drop-in --config-dir files, and command-line flag precedence) and is serialized exactly like /configz.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

See kubernetes/kubernetes#122736.

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Some AI was used

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Kubelet logs effective configuration on start.

ACTION REQUIRED: cluster admin should review permissions to only allow trusted users to nodes/logs cluster role. This is mostly the reminder as it was the best practice anyways and almost all of the effective configuration values can be already Inferred from other log messages or the kubelet behavior.
```

138671.title: kubectl: deprecate run filename flag
138671.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind deprecation
#### What this PR does / why we need it:
`kubectl run` registers `--filename/-f` through `DeleteFlags`, but the run command does not consume `FilenameOptions`.
The command still builds the generated Pod from command-line arguments such as `NAME` and `--image`, and ignores the file passed through `--filename/-f`.
This PR starts the deprecation process for `kubectl run --filename/-f`.
#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Follow-up to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138632
#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This follows up on maintainer feedback from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138632#issuecomment-4333274675.
The scope is intentionally limited to `--filename/-f`.
#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Deprecated the ignored `--filename`/`-f` flag on `kubectl run`.
```

136271.title: cleanup: Remove unused PodStatusResult type
136271.body:
The PodStatusResult type in pkg/apis/core is defined but not referenced anywhere.

  #### What type of PR is this?

  /kind cleanup
  /kind api-change

  #### What this PR does / why we need it:

  This PR removes the unused `PodStatusResult` type from the Kubernetes API.

  **Background:**
  - `PodStatusResult` was introduced in January 2015 ([PR #3565](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/3565)) as a wrapper type for encoding/decoding pod status returned by kubelet's `/podInfo` endpoint
  - Just 4 months later (May 2015), the `/podInfo` endpoint was removed when kubelet architecture changed to push status updates directly to the API server
  - The type has been completely unused for over 10 years
  - It was never exposed via any REST API endpoint to users

  **Why remove it:**
  - The type is vestigial and serves no purpose
  - Any change to Pod status fields (like adding new fields) causes unnecessary test fixture churn for this unused type (see [#135196](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135196))
  - Removing it reduces maintenance burden and codebase complexity

  **Changes:**
  - Removed `PodStatusResult` struct from `pkg/apis/core/types.go` and `staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go`
  - Removed type registration from both internal and versioned scheme
  - Deleted all test fixtures for `core.v1.PodStatusResult`
  - Updated integration tests that referenced this type

  #### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:

  Fixes #136250

  #### Special notes for your reviewer:

  This type was never user-facing - it had no REST endpoint and was only used internally for kubelet-to-apiserver communication via an endpoint that was removed in 2015. Direct removal is appropriate since:
  1. No deprecation period is needed for types that were never exposed to users
  2. There are no external consumers that could be affected
  3. The type has been unused for 10+ years

  The original PR #3565 comment from @bgrant0607: "This is an intermediate state in the path towards just exposing the pod API in Kubelet" - that path was completed long ago.

136709.title: DRA: improve CEL error message for "no such key" errors
136709.body:
## What this PR does

This PR improves the error message when CEL selectors access non-existent device attributes. When users write expressions like `device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"` without checking if the attribute exists first, they currently get a generic "no such key" error with no guidance on how to fix it.

## Why this approach

### String matching for error detection

We detect "no such key" errors using `strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "no such key:")` instead of `errors.Is()` because:
- cel-go's `resolutionError` type is not exported (internal package)
- The cel-go library wraps errors in `types.Err` which only forwards the error message
- Kubernetes itself uses this pattern in apiextensions-apiserver (`staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/schema/cel/validation.go:759`)

### Why these three allocator files

The modification is applied to three allocator variants:
- `structured/internal/stable/allocator_stable.go`
- `structured/internal/incubating/allocator_incubating.go`
- `structured/internal/experimental/allocator_experimental.go`

These three files represent different maturity levels of the DRA allocator implementation. They must be kept in sync because:
1. They are the core CEL selector evaluation points in DRA
2. Features rotate between them as they mature (experimental → incubating → stable)
3. Maintaining consistency ensures behavior is preserved during rotation

### Error message references documentation

The enhanced error message links to `pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/resource/v1#CELDeviceSelector` instead of hardcoding examples. This ensures the error guidance stays current as the CEL documentation evolves with the codebase.

### Documentation improvements

We added concrete examples to `CELDeviceSelector` showing how to handle optional attributes using `orValue()`, `has()`, and the `?` operator. These examples demonstrate the robust patterns users should adopt to avoid "no such key" errors.

## Release note

```release-note
Improved CEL error messages in Dynamic Resource Allocation to provide guidance when accessing non-existent device attributes. Error messages now link to documentation on handling optional fields using orValue() and has().
```

## Related Issue

Fixes #135661

## Test

Added unit tests in `errors_test.go` to verify error enhancement behavior.

#### What type of PR is this?

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
When multiple StorageClasses have the default annotation, `kubectl get storageclass` was showing all of them as "(default)". 
However, only the most recently created one is the effective default.

This PR introduces a custom `TableConvertor` for StorageClass that determines the effective default and only marks that one with "(default)".

**Before:**
```
$ kubectl get storageclass
NAME                   PROVISIONER                                   RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
nfs-client (default)   k8s-sigs.io/nfs-subdir-external-provisioner   Delete          Immediate           false                  3s
standard (default)     kubernetes.io/host-path                       Delete          Immediate           false                  42s
```


**After:**
```
$ kubectl get storageclass
NAME                   PROVISIONER                                   RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
nfs-client (default)   k8s-sigs.io/nfs-subdir-external-provisioner   Delete          Immediate           false                  4s
standard               kubernetes.io/host-path                       Delete          Immediate           false                  14s
```

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #134568

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

The existing `printStorageClass` and `printStorageClassList` in `pkg/printers/internalversion/printers.go` process each StorageClass individually, so they cannot determine which one is the effective default. 
A custom `TableConvertor` was needed to access the full list of StorageClasses and compare their creation timestamps before generating the table.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Fixed kubectl get storageclass to show only the effective default StorageClass as "(default)" when multiple StorageClasses have the default annotation.
```

137141.title: Fix dbus connection leak in node shutdown manager causing thread exhaustion
137141.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When the node shutdown manager's `start()` method fails after creating a dbus connection (e.g., `CurrentInhibitDelay()` returns an error), the connection is never closed. The infinite retry loop in `Start()` keeps creating new connections, each spawning goroutines in the godbus library that never get cleaned up. Over time this leads to thread exhaustion and kubelet crash.

This PR fixes two connection leak paths:

1. **On error:** Uses a `success` flag with `defer` to close the dbus connection if `start()` fails after creating it.
2. **On reconnect:** Explicitly closes the old `m.dbusCon` before replacing it with a new one.

Additionally, `NewDBusCon()` is changed from `dbus.SystemBus()` (shared/cached singleton) to `dbus.ConnectSystemBus()` (private connection). The godbus library explicitly warns that `Close()` must not be called on shared connections returned by `SystemBus()`. `ConnectSystemBus()` creates an independent, authenticated connection that is safe to close.

129109.title: restmapper + discovery: add context-aware APIs
129109.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The main purpose is to replace context.TODO with a context provided by the caller. A secondary purpose is to enable contextual logging.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110810

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119813

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Modifying the existing interfaces and APIs would have a big impact on the ecosystem. This is a no-go. Instead, the following approach was taken:

- All interfaces get duplicated in a *WithContext variant where the methods also have a *WithContext suffix and the ctx parameter. All methods are treated this way except for obvious local get methods (like RESTClient) because it cannot be ruled out entirely that some implementation may need a context.

- Implementations of these interfaces implement both method variants, which is possible because the method names are different. The old methods are implemented as thin wrappers around the updated code which is now the body of the new methods or shared helpers. In some cases there is additional overhead (type checks, potentially additional allocations) when using the old methods.

- `*2Context` helpers bridge from the old to the new interfaces. They try a type cast first. Because the in-tree implementations implement both, they can be used directly. For other implementations wrappers are used.

- None of old APIs and interfaces are marked as deprecated. Instead  doc comments inform consumers about the new and better alternatives.    This approach avoids causing turmoil in the ecosystem when linters    pick up on a formal deprecation and developers act on those linter    warnings without properly thinking about the implications.
    
  "// Contextual logging: " is used as placeholder for "//logcheck:context".      Once all relevant consumers have been updated to the new API,       a search/replace can enable the logcheck linter to warn about       usage of the old API.
    
  Implementations also get marked this way even if probably nothing  ever calls them directly because it shows which code, at least   theoretically, could get removed.

- Existing unit tests do not get updated to the new APIs. This gives us unit test coverage of the old and new API because the old APIs call the new ones.

- In-tree consumers will be updated in follow-up PRs. This is likely to be a longer process. Because of the deprecation comment, `hack/golangci-lint.sh -n` can be used to find code which needs to be updated.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
client-go now has context-aware APIs for REST mapping and discovery. This addresses a long-standing problem that the implementations under the hood made blocking API calls with `context.TODO`. Consumers of client-go are encouraged to switch to the new APIs and therefore they get marked as `Deprecated`. However, there is no plan to ever remove the old APIs.
```

138351.title: optional tracking and documentation of breaking Go API changes in client-go
138351.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind documentation

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The purpose is two-fold:
- Raise awareness during PR review that a PR includes a breaking Go API change, as reported by apidiff ("incompatible change"). Previously, contributors and reviewers had to pay attention to the non-blocking apidiff jobs or catch changes manually.
- Document in client-go/CHANGELOG.md and apimachinery/CHANGELOG.md (disabled in a later commit, see individual commits for what it would look like) which breaking changes were made and how (if necessary) consumers of those packages can adapt to those changes. Previously they had to figure that out based on the source code diff and maybe some comments in the PR which made those changes.

As proof-of-concept, information about the changes in Kubernetes 1.35 and 1.36 are included. No attempt was made to explain the changes, they only include the title of the PR and a link to it. See commits for information how this was done automatically. We could go back further, if desired.

This is implemented in hack/apidiff.sh. Developers who are making a breaking change can use `hack/update-go-apidocs.sh` to add a new changelog entry. They still need to edit it before submitting the PR. The `hack/verify-go-apidocs.sh` checks that, but currently never fails (= not enforced yet, will be enabled in the future).

N/A

@aojea, @skitt: this works pretty much as proposed at the meet&greet at KubeCon EU 2026.

@aojea's [dumping of the current public API](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137270) is orthogonal to this.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138359 demonstrates how this would work in a PR which changes the client-go API.

138575.title: Promote Workload API to v1alpha3 and remove v1alpha2
138575.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In release 1.36, we introduced initial changes to the Workload API (including `Workload` and `PodGroup` objects) in the `v1alpha2` version of the `scheduling.k8s.io` API group. For the 1.37 release, we plan to make further changes to these APIs and eventually promote them to Beta.
To follow Kubernetes API best practices and allow for breaking changes in the next iteration without maintaining multiple alpha versions, we need to create a new `v1alpha3` version as a copy of `v1alpha2`. We will migrate all internal consumers to `v1alpha3` and remove `v1alpha2` in this release. This avoids the overhead of maintaining both versions with conversion logic for an experimental API, while allowing us to evolve the API.

### Why is this needed?

We would like to promote the Workload API to `v1alpha3` and remove `v1alpha2` by performing the following steps:
1.  **Create `v1alpha3` API Definitions**:
    *   Copy `staging/src/k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3`.
    *   Copy `pkg/apis/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3`.
    *   Update package names and references to point to the new `v1alpha3`.
2.  **Remove `v1alpha2` API Definitions**:
    *   Delete the old `v1alpha2` directories in both `staging` and `pkg/apis`.
3.  **Update Internal References**:
    *   Update all imports and usages of `k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2` to `v1alpha3` across the repository (e.g., in `pkg/scheduler/`, `plugin/pkg/admission/`).
4.  **Code Generation**:
    *   Run Kubernetes code generators to create clientsets, informers, listers, and deepcopy functions for the new version.

135661.title: DRA: Scheduler CEL evaluation fails with "no such key" when accessing nested attributes without existence check
135661.body:
### What happened?

I am using DRA with a CEL selector to filter devices based on driver attributes. When writing an expression that accesses a nested field within `device.attributes`, the scheduler encounters a CEL runtime error if the specific driver key does not exist on the device, rather than evaluating the expression to false.

The following expression fails during the DynamicResources filter plugin execution:

```
cel:
  expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the expression to evaluate to false for devices that do not possess the gpu.nvidia.com attribute, allowing the scheduler to simply skip those devices.

Instead, the scheduler treats this as a hard runtime error, preventing the claim from being allocated even if valid devices exist, or logging significant errors during the filter phase.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: gpu.nvidia.com
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel: 
      expression: "device.driver == 'gpu.nvidia.com'"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceSlice
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-devices-slice
spec:
  nodeName: kind-control-plane
  driver: gpu.nvidia.com

  pool:
    generation: 1
    resourceSliceCount: 1
    name: kind-control-plane-gpu-pool

  devices:
  - name: gpu-0
    bindsToNode: true

  - name: gpu-1
    attributes:
      sharingStrategy:
        string: runai-fractions
    bindsToNode: true
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - name: gpu-runai-fractionable
      exactly:
        deviceClassName: gpu.nvidia.com
        capacity:
          requests:
            memory: 10Gi
        selectors:
        - cel:
            expression: 'device.attributes["gpu.nvidia.com"].sharingStrategy == "runai-fractions"'
---

  name: fraction-pod-1

  resourceClaims:
  - name: fraction-claim
    resourceClaimName: kind-control-plane-gpu-runai-fractionable-claim-1

  - name: fraction-container
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: fraction-claim
    image: ubuntu:latest
    command: [ "/bin/bash", "-c", "--" ]
    args: [sleep Infinity"]
```

Almost everywhere we check whether a pod has pod level resources (PLRs) we don't differentiate between nil and empty PLRs. For example:

```yaml
  resources: {}

      image: registry.k8s.io/pause:latest

        requests:
          cpu:    100m
          memory: 50Mi
        limits:
          cpu:    100m

```

I'm not sure exactly what the implications of this are, but since it breaks some fundamental assumptions, it's probably not good.

What was the reason for ignoring empty pod level resources?

We'll need to be careful about backwards compatibility when fixing this.

120181.title: job executions started manually for a cronjob are marked as unexpected
120181.body:
### What happened?

We have a custom resource with a name - `Foo`
We have a CronJob named - `Foo`

Now, we have a job whose owner refernce is set to the custom resource name - `Foo`. We have noticed that the job when stopped (suspended) basically causes an event/warning - "[UnexpectedJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L444C39-L444C55)" for the given job execution.

[syncCronJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L422C25-L422C36) is trying to reconcile the job because it thinks that it is owned by the CronJob. Probably because of "[getJobsToBeReconciled](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L252C25-L252C46)", at this [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L264C3-L264C110).

### What did you expect to happen?

The `syncCronJob` should not try to reconcile the job because it is not owned by the CronJob. 

**Proposed Solution**: [syncCronJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8b132ea40a250e9acf08ab2fadb9a8c2fd811d74/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L422C25-L422C36) should not reconcile the job, since it is owned by the CronJob. The `getJobsToBeReconciled` method should match the `name` and the `kind` of the job. The `kind` in the case of a cronjob would be `CronJob`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Run a job execution using the same CRD used to create a cronjob.
- Once the job execution starts, stop (suspend) it.
- We would start getting events of type `Warning` with reason - `UnexpectedJob`.

135988.title: ImageVolume: Empty image.reference in Pod templates passes API validation but fails at runtime
135988.body:
### What happened?

When creating a Deployment or StatefulSet with an ImageVolume that has an empty `image.reference` field, the API validation passes, but Pod creation fails at runtime. This creates a confusing user experience where workloads appear to be created successfully but never produce running Pods

**Direct Pod creation correctly rejects empty reference:**

```
$ k apply -f pod-with-empty-ref.yaml
The Pod "test" is invalid: spec.volumes[0].image.reference: Required value
```

**But Deployment/StatefulSet incorrectly accepts it:**

```
$ k apply -f deployment-with-empty-ref.yaml
deployment.apps/test-imagevolume-empty-ref created  # Should have been rejected
```

The error only appears in Events when the ReplicaSet controller tries to create Pods:

```
Warning  FailedCreate  replicaset-controller  Error creating: Pod "..." is invalid:
  [spec.volumes[0].image.reference: Required value, ...]
```

### What did you expect to happen?

API validation should reject empty `image.reference` in Pod templates (Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, etc.), not just in direct Pod creation.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a kind cluster with Kubernetes v1.35+:

```bash
$ kind create cluster --name test
```

2. Apply this Deployment:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-imagevolume-empty-ref
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test
  template:
```

136831.title: StatefulSet function completeRollingUpdate does not check AvailableReplicas (minReadySeconds bug)
136831.body:
### What happened?

When a StatefulSet has `minReadySeconds` configured, the `completeRollingUpdate` function prematurely marks the rolling update as complete. It sets `status.CurrentRevision = status.UpdateRevision` as soon as all replicas are Ready, without waiting for them to be Available (i.e., Ready for at least `minReadySeconds`).

### What did you expect to happen?

The rolling update should not be considered complete until all replicas are both Ready and Available (have been Ready for at least minReadySeconds).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a StatefulSet with minReadySeconds set to a non-zero value (e.g., 60s)
2. Trigger a rolling update
3. Observe that status.CurrentRevision is updated to status.UpdateRevision before pods have been Available for at least minReadySeconds

### Anything else we need to know?

Root cause:

In function [completeRollingUpdate](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.35.0/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_utils.go#L638-L647), the condition checks ReadyReplicas but not AvailableReplicas:

```go
func completeRollingUpdate(set *apps.StatefulSet, status *apps.StatefulSetStatus) {
	if set.Spec.UpdateStrategy.Type == apps.RollingUpdateStatefulSetStrategyType &&
		status.UpdatedReplicas == *set.Spec.Replicas &&
		status.ReadyReplicas == *set.Spec.Replicas &&
		status.Replicas == *set.Spec.Replicas {
		status.CurrentReplicas = status.UpdatedReplicas
		status.CurrentRevision = status.UpdateRevision
	}
}
```


The fix is to add status.AvailableReplicas == *set.Spec.Replicas to the condition. This was originally identified in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122272#discussion_r1526750533.

Kubernetes version: all versions since StatefulSetMinReadySeconds graduated to GA (v1.27+)

### What would you like to be added?

With cluster events, we need to check whether we can requeue unschedulable pods into active queue or backoff queue more efficiently.

/assign

### Why is this needed?

When it comes to gang scheduling, when Pod/Add event happens, it should also check unschedulable pods (because the newly added pod, along with unschedulable pods grouped together may complete the gang/workload).

Workaround was introduced is to use "MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue()" inside the "Add/Pod" cluster event. But this would run queuing hints for all plugins subscribing to such event, while we are only concerned with "GangScheduling" plugin for this particular case.

### References

A relevant issue was mentioned earlier in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127290 and has pull request that wasn't merged/accepted https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127387 because it adds many lines of code and there was no strong reason to do so.

But with gang scheduling being introduced, this seems to be beneficial.

123559.title: kube-proxy: Inconsistent behaviors about disabling health check server and metrics server
123559.body:
### What happened?

While looking at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123545, I tried to validate the current behaviors about "healthz-bind-address" and "metrics-bind-address", and found some inconsistencies between the docs and the code.

1. According to the following usages, setting "--healthz-bind-address" and "--metrics-bind-address" to empty values should disable the two servers, however making such configurations doesn't really work. So it's either a doc issue or a code issue.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54f9807e1e84981b2053f4daf779f5ed19962144/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L163-L164

2. Regardless of whether disabling the two servers should be supported or not, the validation code for the two addresses are inconsistent, it tolerates HealthzBindAddress to be empty but not MetricsBindAddress. kube-proxy wouldn't be up when MetricsBindAddress is empty.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54f9807e1e84981b2053f4daf779f5ed19962144/pkg/proxy/apis/config/validation/validation.go#L73-L76

3. `HealthzServer` is only initialized when `HealthzBindAddress` is not empty. However, it's used by `NodeEligibleHandler` unconditionally, which would cause kube-proxy to panic when it's nil.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54f9807e1e84981b2053f4daf779f5ed19962144/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L644-L646
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/54f9807e1e84981b2053f4daf779f5ed19962144/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L954-L956

It seems that regardless of whether we want to support disabling the two servers, some cleanup would be needed. But I'm not sure what's the expected behavior here.

cc @danwinship @aojea 

/sig network
/area kube-proxy

### What did you expect to happen?

The documented way to disable health check server and metrics server doesn't work. If it's a real use case, it should be fixed. Otherwise, the usage doc should be fixed.
